Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear asks. High-level answer below and I attached a brief pricing appendix (redwood_pricing_appendix_Q4_v2.pdf) with worked examples. TL;DR: we support an "annual bucket" commitment with quarterly true-ups and a configurable burst cushion; discounts are tiered and apply to committed tokens first, then to overage tokens at distinct overage rates.

Summary (concise):
- Annualized bucket: customer commits to an annual token quantity (e.g., 1B tokens). We split this into 4 seasonal buckets for operational headroom (default equal quarters unless you provide a monthly curve).
- Burst cushion: by default we include a 10% annual burst window that can be applied to any quarter; you may choose to increase to 15% for a higher commitment tier. Burst usage is charged from the cushion first and then from overage rates.
- Quarterly true-up: at the end of each quarter we reconcile committed vs actual consumption. If utilization is below the committed bucket for the quarter, credits can be reserved to a one-quarter buffer before being forfeit (configurable).
- Discounting & overages: committed tokens receive the committed per-token price (tiered). Overages are billed at a higher overage rate; however, we offer staged overage discounts based on annualized attainment bands (see attached discount_matrix.xlsx).

Example (from appendix):
- Annual commit: 1,000,000,000 tokens (commit rate $0.00008/token)
- Burst cushion: 10% (100,000,000 tokens)
- Q3 unexpected peak: 200,000,000 tokens used
  - 100M covered by cushion (no overage rate)
  - Remaining 100M billed as overage at $0.00012/token, but if annual attainment crosses 110% we step down to $0.00010/token for that tranche per the staircase discount.

I'll work with Marissa on the exact contract language and a consolidated reply with suggested clause text. Sending internal note next to loop in LAuren for billing/legal.

Karthik / team — draft concession language below and I attached a discount matrix workbook (discount_matrix.xlsx) with the stepped bands. Key recommendation: offer a two-tier graceband and a single proactive concession to close the deal quickly.

Draft MSA paragraph (proposed):
"Bucketized Annual Commitment and Burst Cushion: Customer will commit to an Annual Token Commitment (ATC). The ATC will be allocated across four billing quarters (Quarter Allocation). Redwood will provide a Burst Cushion equal to 10% of ATC by default. Burst Cushion usage will be applied prior to overage billing. At each calendar quarter end, Redwood will perform a True-Up comparing actual consumption against the Quarter Allocation. Any unused tokens in a prior quarter may be carried forward to the next single quarter up to a maximum carryforward equal to 5% of ATC (Carryforward Cap). Unused tokens beyond the Carryforward Cap are forfeited unless otherwise agreed in writing.

Discounting Approach: Committed tokens are billed at the Committed Rate as defined in Schedule A. Overages are billed at the Overage Rate, subject to annual attainment-based discounts (Stepped Attainment Discounts). Where annual consumption exceeds 100% of ATC, Redwood will apply a retroactive attainment adjustment to committed and overage tranches per the Discount Matrix attached.

Proposed commercial concession (limited time): If MediCore signs within 30 days of the attached proposal, Redwood will apply a one-time Onboarding Credit equal to 0.5% of the ATC billed value, which will be applied to first-quarter invoices.

Ben: for billing wording, recommend we be explicit that cushion consumption is reported on monthly invoices as "Burst Cushion Usage" with a separate line item so it's auditable.

If no redlines from legal, I suggest we send this back to Samantha with the appendix.

Marissa Cole
